issue_text: Hi, I need the full details for my round-trip airline reservation C4C633. Please include the complete itinerary, both passengers currently on the booking, how many bags are already attached, whether insurance is included, and the payment history. Also, while you're in that reservation, please check the current status of the outbound flight FLE7F420 for 2026-10-01 and tell me whether that segment still looks normal.
summary: An eight-turn session across airline, messaging, and retail skills, largely on one user's reservations. The baseline signature is confirmation-gated and verification-heavy: the agent pre-confirms before each mutation, works directly against SQLite when the ORM won't validate, and reads state back afterward. It reasons sharply about no-ops — twice it recognizes a requested 'update' is identical to current state and declines to make a pointless change — and recalls prior results across turns. The baseline weakness is its handling of anomalous data: a $0-paid reservation is explained by unverified speculation and a travel date absent from the flight schedule is still pronounced 'normal'. In this control condition nothing challenges those judgments, so they stand unreviewed.

findings.title: Correct no-op recognition
findings.body: Asked to 'update' passengers and later to 'change' flights to values identical to the booking, the agent compares against current state and declines to act — a clean Reasoning › Match + Deciding no-op rather than a spurious mutation.

findings.title: Confirm-then-mutate with direct-DB fallback
findings.body: Every change is pre-confirmed and verified; when the ORM fails validation the agent writes SQLite directly 'the same way the tool would', keeping Planning › fallback and Executing active.

findings.title: Anomalies explained away, not resolved
findings.body: A $0-paid booking is attributed to a possible certificate/voucher 'may reflect...' with no check, and a Sep-16 date missing from the flight schedule is still judged 'normal'.
